sources.entry: µTask - Automation engine that models and executes business processes declared in yaml. BSD-3-Clause Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: µTask is a lightweight automation engine that runs business processes declared as YAML task templates, with only a Postgres database required.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you describe a process as a YAML task template: a set of inputs plus a graph of steps with dependencies, conditions, loops and retries. The engine executes each step asynchronously, retries transient errors, and keeps an encrypted, auditable trace of intermediate states until the task completes. Built-in action types include http, ssh, email, notify, subtask/batch, script, tag, cache and an OVH API call. Custom action plugins and init plugins are written in Go and compiled as .so files. Task state changes can be sent to Slack, Opsgenie, or generic webhooks. Multiple instances coordinate through a single Postgres database, and a dashboard and HTTP API are provided.
use_cases: Automate multi-step provisioning workflows such as creating accounts or certificates
Run asynchronous back-office processes that need human approval or input forms
Orchestrate HTTP API calls with retries and conditional branching
Schedule and track long-running jobs with an auditable history
Use as a task backend for other services via tags and the API
Chain scripts, SSH commands and notifications into one tracked workflow
how_to_run: Download the install script (URL missing from the README text), then run: sh install-utask.sh
Alternatively, clone the repository and run: make all
notable: Workflows are declared in YAML with step dependencies, conditional skip/check logic, and custom states
Loops via foreach with parallel or sequential strategies
Built-in resource limits (semaphores) to throttle concurrency per target
Encryption of stored data with a documented key-rotation procedure
Extensible through Go action plugins and reusable function templates
caveats: Authentication is not built in: it expects a reverse proxy to supply an x-remote-user header; basic-auth is for development only
Requires writing Go and compiling .so plugins for custom actions, and Docker-based packaging for deployment
Only Postgres 9.5 or newer is supported as the database
